from textkit import count_words, reverse_words, slugify


class CoreTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_count_words(self):
        self.assertEqual(count_words("a b  c"), 3)
        self.assertEqual(count_words(""), 0)

        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello  World"), "hello-world")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello_World"), "hello-world")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("hello-world"), "hello-world")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---hello---world---"), "hello-world")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello, World!"), "hello-world")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("123 ABC"), "123-abc")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")

def slugify(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert text to a URL-friendly slug.
    
    Lowercases the input, replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters
    with single dashes, and strips leading/trailing dashes.
    
    Args:
        text: The text to convert to a slug.
        
    Returns:
        A URL-friendly slug string containing only lowercase letters,
        digits, and dashes.
        
    Examples:
        >>> slugify("Hello World")
        'hello-world'
        >>> slugify("Hello  World")  # Multiple spaces become single dash
        'hello-world'
        >>> slugify("---hello---world---")  # Leading/trailing dashes removed
        'hello-world'
        >>> slugify("Hello, World!")  # Punctuation replaced with dash
        'hello-world'
        >>> slugify("Hello_World")  # Underscores treated as separators
        'hello-world'
        >>> slugify("")  # Empty string returns empty
        ''
    """
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', text)
    text = text.strip('-')
    return text
